messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the torch 2.6.3 + driver 535.x roll last night we saw a persistent small-batch tail latency spike (2-3x) on KV-heavy workloads. CI prefetch-affinity stress tests failed during the canary rollout.

ci-bot: nightly-kv-prefetch-stress | FAILURE | job: canary-prefetch-affinity | link: https://ci.internal/runs/4829 | first-failing-step: perf/smoke/smallbatch-tail

jon: Do we have a reproducer on staging? Which metric exactly spiked (p50/p95/p99)?

maria: p50 unchanged, p95 up ~1.8x, p99 up ~3x. Repro on staging with synthetic KV traces that mimic customer L. I ran the stress harness for ~30m and saw periodic thrash every ~90s.

ash: Could be kernel selection flipping under new nvrtc/driver. Did autotune table change? Any kernel flips in logs?

sam: I pulled triton/autotune logs from the failing run. There's a lot of matmul kernel churn around small batch sizes and then prefetch threads get stacked up. Snippet: ```[2026-03-10T03:12:14Z] autotune: selected kernel matmul_fuse_v2_grid32_x128 for input (B=2, S=64)
[2026-03-10T03:12:14Z] prefetch: spawn_worker(12)
[2026-03-10T03:12:14Z] autotune: selected kernel matmul_fuse_v1_grid16_x64 for input (B=2, S=64)
[2026-03-10T03:12:15Z] prefetch: worker(12) blocked on eviction lock
```

jon: That eviction lock line is worrying. Could be a change in our KV prefetch affinity heuristics + driver's warp scheduler -> longer critical sections. Any prof samples?

maria: I grabbed a short perf profile from staging. Main hotspots: 
- prefetch_worker::prepare_request (40%)
- allocator::try_evict_range (25%)
- cudaKernelLauncher (15%)
- triton::matmul_dispatch (10%)

Also saw increased cudaStreamSynchronize time in the p99 traces.

ash: If allocator try_evict_range is that hot, prefetch workers are contending on shard locks. Maybe the driver/torch change increased kernel latencies causing prefetch backlog -> more eviction churn.

ci-bot: flaky-regression-detector | regression: smallbatch-tail | signal: +2.3x p99 on cuda-535 + torch-2.6.3 (replicated in staging)

sam: Quick check: rolling back to torch 2.6.2 + driver 534 on a staging node removed the periodic thrash in 40m run. So reproducer seems tied to environment bump.

jon: Let's bisect the surface: is it torch's nvrtc runtime codegen change or driver scheduling? We should try: (A) torch 2.6.3 + driver 534, (B) torch 2.6.2 + driver 535. Run short stress on each.

maria: I can run (A) tonight. Can someone take (B)? If (B) fails then it's driver. If (A) fails then it's torch.

ash: I'll queue (B) on a spare node. Also adding `--prefetch-workers=8` vs `--prefetch-workers=2` to test if lowering concurrency masks it (could be contention).

sam: FYI captured a stackdump during a stall, sample: ```thread 0x7f9 prefetch_worker::run -> evict_lock -> cudaStreamSynchronize -> matmul_kernel_entry``` Looks like CPU thread waiting on stream which in turn is slow.

jon: Good. If kernel latency increased, autotune might oscillate and produce suboptimal kernels, causing more synchronizations. We should also collect per-kernel durations (cuLaunch + completion) across versions.

maria: Action items: 
- I will run (A) torch2.6.3 + driver534 tonight and post results (maria).
- Ash will run (B) torch2.6.2 + driver535 and try lower prefetch-workers (ash).
- Jon will add a quick perf hook to record cuLaunch->completion latencies and autotune selection histogram (jon).
- Sam will try a temporary revert of the small autotune heuristic change from last week in a staging binary and run the harness (sam).

ash: If we confirm driver is root cause, we should gate the canary and open a ticket with vendor with perf traces. If torch is root cause, revert the NVRTC/device-linker patch.

maria: Also flagging this as a rollout blocker for the next 24h until we know which axis it is. Will update thread with logs. :eyes:

ci-bot: created issue perf/2259: "smallbatch tail latency regression after torch2.6.3/driver535" (assignees: maria, jon) https://issue.internal/2259

jon: Thanks — tagging infra to hold the rollout. I'll start the instrumentation PR now.

maria: Update (1h): ran (A) — torch2.6.3 + driver534 — no regression in 45m stress. Ash's (B) looks failed within 6m. Preliminary conclusion: driver 535 is the primary suspect.

ash: Confirmed (B) failure. Lowering prefetch-workers to 2 reduces amplitude but doesn't eliminate p99 shift. Dumping kernel durations now and will attach to issue.

sam: I'll prepare a hotfix: pin the canary fleet to driver 534 and block 535 until vendor response. Drafting rollback playbook.

maria: Good work. If anyone finds a quick mitigation (tunes to autotune or prefetch backoff) post to the ticket, otherwise hold the rollout and let's escalate to vendor with traces. :locked_with_key:
